newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MAY 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MAY 22.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The government is worried about the extent of its law-making abilities given the activity of internal party dissenters who are developing into a watchdog of traditional ruling party PASOK values. Senior government officials say they are facing a serious problem in the ranks of PASOK MPs.

--The government is under pressure from international organisations to enforce an even stricter economic regime, with the IMF and the OECD calling for tighter wage and social security and pension policies.

--A rash of attacks by marauding Albanian pirates and bandits on locals and tourists off Corfu has raised concerns of the repercussions on tourism. The Greek National Tourist Organisation and tour operators are keeping a low profile despite the reports of foreign media.

--High school teachers are about to reject Education Minister Gerasimos Arsenis's reforms for the high school curriculum. A 12-day training seminar on using the new methods - no textbooks, but a dossier on subjects - will be given to teachers.
--A school official was suspended from duties yesterday after he recommended schools not teach Kazantzakis's works becaue his works are "blasphemous".

--A policeman stationed at Greece's Gjirokaster consulate confessed yesterday to killing his colleague Nikos Markakis with a single shot to the face on Tuesday. Dimitris Tzavellas told police they were playing with their guns when his went off.
--An cacophony of voices - Prime Minister Costas Simitis's advisor, IMF and OECD - are recommending further austerity with wage restraint, pension reforms and an increase in lay-offs.
--Mobile phone suppliers have declared a pricing war ahead of national telecommunications organisation OTE's entry into the fray in September. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
